I will still do it the way that has worked for me here, just a bit tighter on money because my land is only 1.1 mu and every bag I buy shows up in the household spending. On this kind of wheat-maize land in Quzhou, I do not start from zero. I look at what I used last year, then I watch what the nearby families are doing on fields with well water like mine. If I change too much and the yield drops, that loss hurts more than spending a little extra on fertilizer. So for wheat, I will keep an improved variety, put the main fertilizer under before sowing, and use well water at the key times: before winter if dry, at jointing, and at grain filling if needed. Wheat needs to stand strong through winter, so I will not cut nitrogen too hard. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives better ears here when water is available. I will put part of the fertilizer at planting and the rest around the big bell-mouth stage, because if maize runs short then, the yield falls fast. Since my area is small, I can manage with family labor and spray on time, so I will keep pesticide use to the common local pattern: one or two times if pressure is light, more only if I really see trouble. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on a small plot after each crop and cheaper than deep ploughing every season. With well irrigation, decent seed, and fertilizer a little on the safe side, I will aim for a steady harvest instead of gambling on saving one small bag of input.
